summary: Technical sync between Redwood and Velos to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private/dedicated deploys, joint solution onboarding flow, and benchmark plan. Action items assigned for staging, docs, and security checklist.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood Product), Aisha Rahman (Velos Head of Partnerships), Tom Becker (Velos PM), Diego Morales (Velos Cloud Architect), Lena Fischer (Velos Security)

[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining. i think we've got about 45 minutes. quick intros?
[00:00:08] Aisha: hi all, Aisha here, head of partnerships at Velos. excited to go through the tech bits.
[00:00:12] Tom: tom, PM on the marketplace side. i'll be owning the listing integration.
[00:00:15] Priya: priya from redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll lead the arch discussion.
[00:00:18] Marcus: marcus, product. good to meet you all.
[00:00:22] Diego: diego, cloud architect, i'll handle networking and infra constraints.
[00:00:25] Lena: lena from security, i'll focus on compliance and kms questions.
[00:00:28] Jordan: awesome. goal today: align on what Velos needs for a marketplace listing and the joint reference architecture for private/dedicated deploys, plus scope a benchmark.
[00:00:40] Tom: high level, marketplace wants a listing that supports both hosted api offering and a dedicated/private option. we'll need a manifest with deployment options, icons, screenshots, pricing model, and an onboarding flow that can provision a test instance in our staging environment.
[00:00:58] Jordan: got it. from redwood side we typically surface hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity and private vpc installs. for marketplace i think we can expose hosted + dedicated as standard, and list private as contact-sales with reference architecture.
[00:01:15] Priya: quick note - private deployments often need a reference arch showing VPC peering, subnets, KMS integration, and ingress rules. i'll sketch a diagram during this call.
[00:01:29] Diego: important for us: our marketplace runs in customers' VPCs and we need to know if redwood supports cross-account VPC peering or needs a customer-managed connector. also what's the default egress pattern and ports?
[00:01:45] Priya: yes, redwood private supports customer-managed VPC peering and also a connector model. default ports are 443 for control plane and a data plane port range for gRPC; i'll list exact ports in the doc.
[00:01:58] Lena: on security, we need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS options - can customers bring their own KMS/HSM? also audit logs for inference calls - retention windows?
[00:02:11] Marcus: we support BYOK with standard KMS integrations, and audit logs can be exported to customer cloud logging; retention configurable, default 30 days in hosted but enterprise can ask for longer.
[00:02:25] Diego: that works. any network latency implications if we do VPC peering vs connector?
[00:02:32] Priya: peering generally is lower latency; connector introduces a hop but can be optimized. for latency-sensitive customers we recommend peering plus local GPU hosts (dedicated). we'll include expected latency ranges in the reference sheet but benchmarks will be definitive.
[00:02:50] Aisha: marketplace listing will require a short reference architecture doc and a list of supported regions/hardware. do you have a standard set of instance types you recommend?
[00:03:00] Marcus: we publish recommended profiles: small inference (cpu or single A10/NVIDIA T4), production throughput (A100/H100 depending on model), and dedicated GPU pools. for marketplace we can provide a simplified table mapping model families to recommended footprints.
[00:03:16] Tom: also need a demo flow - can we offer a sandbox credential that provisions a temporary hosted endpoint for Velos users to try the integration?
[00:03:25] Jordan: yes we can provide a dev sandbox token and a sample project. Priya, will that require any special infra?
[00:03:31] Priya: no special infra; we can spin up a temp hosted instance. for private/dedicated we can do a demo via a constrained staging account on velos. we'll need staging credentials to provision resources.
[00:03:42] Tom: we'll create the staging marketplace sandbox, share creds with you. action item noted.
[00:03:48] Diego: about billing - marketplace expects usage hooks so we can bill customers through Velos. do you expose metering events or usage webhooks?
[00:03:58] Jordan: yes we export per-token metering and per-embedding units as usage events; we can surface a webhook or S3/BigQuery export. we'll also support invoices for dedicated accounts.
[00:04:13] Lena: for SOC2 and audit logs, can we get a runbook or compliance whitepaper to put in the marketplace listing?
[00:04:19] Marcus: absolutely. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and the security whitepaper. note some section might reference radwood in the old draft - apologies for typos, we'll clean it up.
[00:04:30] Aisha: okay re: joint solutions - beyond the listing, we'd like a reference architecture that shows a typical integration for Velos customers: marketplace listing -> provisioning -> VPC peering -> onboarding flow -> monitoring.
[00:04:45] Priya: i'll propose a 3-tier reference arch: 1) Hosted (simple API), 2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in redwood with VPN/peering), 3) Private (on-prem or VPC with BYOK). each will have network diagrams.
[00:04:59] Diego: in the dedicated flow, who manages the GPU instances? are they in redwood-managed accounts or in Velos?
[00:05:06] Jordan: dedicated capacity is hosted in redwood datacenters but can be regionally provisioned; customers commit to capacity. private deployments can be customer-hosted. we'll clarify in the doc.
[00:05:15] Tom: marketplace metadata we'll need: short description, long description, screenshots, pricing tiers, tags, supported regions, security certifications, trial instructions. format is a YAML manifest we will provide.
[00:05:31] Priya: please send the manifest template. we can fill in model names, supported quantization profiles, and recommended batch sizes.
[00:05:38] Aisha: question on quantization and model variants - do you expose quantized models for lower-cost inference on smaller instances?
[00:05:45] Marcus: yes we have quantization profiles and suggest model variants by latency/cost tradeoff. we'll include guidance: e.g., 8-bit quant for throughput cost savings with slight quality tradeoff; also mention automatic fallback to higher-precision models for canary or A/B tests.
[00:06:02] Diego: benchmarks - i'd like to see latency at 1, 5, 20 concurrency and cost per 1M tokens on Velos hardware. can redwood run those benchmarks or do we run them?
[00:06:12] Priya: we usually run initial benchmarks on our side, but for marketplace listing we'll run joint benchmarks on Velos staging to provide realistic numbers. need your staging account for that.
[00:06:21] Jordan: timeline-wise, can we aim to have the draft reference arch and manifest by 2026-03-18, provisioning by 2026-03-17, and benchmarks the week of 2026-03-22?
[00:06:32] Aisha: that timeline works for us.
[00:06:34] Lena: security items - KMS BYOK, data residency, audit logs retention, and SSO (SAML/OIDC) support. how do you handle customer-managed keys?
[00:06:43] Marcus: BYOK is supported via standard KMS integrations and we can integrate with customer HSM via KMIP in private deployments. SSO supported via SAML and OIDC.
[00:06:54] Lena: do you have a data deletion certificate/process for when a customer terminates?
[00:07:00] Priya: yes, we have data lifecycle APIs and deletion certificates - i'll attach the procedural doc.
[00:07:06] Tom: marketplace also requires a support SLA for listed partners; what SLAs do you offer for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:07:14] Jordan: hosted API gets standard support with 99.9% uptime for paid tiers; dedicated has SLA add-ons with guaranteed latency targets and faster incident response. we can share the SLA doc.
[00:07:26] Diego: one technical item - does redwood runtime require GPU drivers or specific kernel versions for private installs? we run mixed kernel baselines.
[00:07:35] Priya: private installs require a supported GPU driver set; we'll attach a compatibility matrix. for containerized installs we recommend gpu driver >= X.Y and kernel >= A.B.
[00:07:46] Aisha: good. any blockers we foresee?
[00:07:49] Priya: the main blocker for the benchmark is staging credentials and network rules; also if Velos enforces restrictive egress we might need a connector pattern.
[00:07:59] Diego: we can open egress to a set of IPs for the test window. i'll coordinate with our network team.
[00:08:05] Jordan: perfect. now, onto listing process details - Tom, what's your expected cadence for approvals?
[00:08:12] Tom: once we have the manifest and security docs, we'll do a review cycle (1 week) and then validation in staging (another week). total ~2 weeks to publish after we have artifacts.
[00:08:23] Marcus: we'll aim to get docs to you within three business days.
[00:08:27] Aisha: content for the listing - can you provide a short blurb and two screenshots of the console and a sample SDK snippet?
[00:08:35] Jordan: yes, we'll provide a short marketing blurb and a technical snippet. priya will take console screenshots from staging.
[00:08:42] Priya: quick note - some of the product names in our older docs get transcribed incorrectly (radwood etc.), we'll ensure the artifacts use correct branding.
[00:08:50] Lena: on compliance, i need the SOC2 cert and the encryption whitepaper to attach to our marketplace compliance page.
[00:08:57] Marcus: i'll attach SOC2 summary and security whitepaper to the next email.
[00:09:02] Diego: for the benchmark, what metrics will you produce? p50/p95 latency, throughput, token cost, and memory footprint?
[00:09:09] Priya: yes p50/p95/p99, token cost per 1M tokens, concurrency scaling curves, and resource utilization. we'll include a short methodology doc.
[00:09:19] Tom: can we also include a quickstart terraform script that provisions the required infra in velos staging? that speeds validation.
[00:09:26] Jordan: we have example terraform modules - we'll adapt them to Velos staging.
[00:09:31] Aisha: excellent. let's capture action items: redwood to send reference arch and manifest; velos to create staging sandbox; both to run benchmarks.
[00:09:40] Jordan: agreed. i'll recap at the end with owners.
[00:09:44] [00:10:00] -- brief mute while sharing screen --
[00:10:45] Priya: (screen) here's a rough diagram: left is Velos customer VPC, right is redwood dedicated pool; peering shown, plus optional connector path; control plane communication over 443, data plane over gRPC range. note: transcript may call this KV cash in places, but it's KV cache.
[00:11:10] Diego: looks good, can you annotate the subnets and security group recommendations?
[00:11:15] Priya: yes, we'll annotate public/private subnets, recommended NAT rules, and the SGs that should be opened.
[00:11:27] Marcus: also including a diagram for the hosted flow - simple API calls to the hosted endpoint with an example token exchange flow.
[00:11:36] Tom: marketplace needs a manifest sample; can you include the deployment_type field with values hosted|dedicated|private?
[00:11:44] Priya: yes we'll include that.
[00:11:47] Lena: on audit logs - can you specify the fields included (user id, api key, timestamp, model, prompt hash) so we can map to our compliance schema?
[00:11:58] Marcus: log fields: request_id, timestamp, user_id, model_id, tokens_in/out, status, latency_ms. prompt text is redacted by default but can be retained under contract; we'll note redaction policy.
[00:12:12] Diego: any gotchas for private installs with certain linux distros?
[00:12:17] Priya: we support a set of distros; RHEL/Centos, Ubuntu LTS are recommended. we'll include a compatibility matrix.
[00:12:25] Aisha: great. switching to the onboarding flow - after a customer clicks install on Velos, what's the sequence?
[00:12:30] Tom: typically: marketplace sends provisioning request -> redwood validates account -> provisioning job runs to create instance or provide connector -> notify marketplace -> user gets dashboard link.
[00:12:40] Jordan: we can implement a webhook from marketplace to kick off provisioning. Priya, is there an idempotent provisioning API?
[00:12:46] Priya: yes, our provisioning api is idempotent with request-id. we'll provide sample calls.
[00:12:52] Diego: for private installs behind strict firewalls, do you support an air-gapped install path?
[00:12:58] Marcus: yes, we have an air-gapped on-prem package but it's a heavier lift; that's normally enterprise and would be handled as a professional services engagement.
[00:13:08] Lena: note that for air-gapped installs, KMS and audit exports require custom setup - we should document that as well.
[00:13:14] Priya: agreed. we'll add a section.
[00:13:18] [00:13:30] Jordan: ok we're about halfway through. any other marketplace constraints?
[00:13:35] Tom: one more: Velos requires a security contact and a support contact listed in the manifest. also a logo with transparent background.
[00:13:44] Aisha: confirmed.
[00:13:46] Diego: small request - can benchmarks include a cold-start number and a warm-start number? some customers care about cold latency.
[00:13:53] Priya: yes we'll report cold vs warm start and include caching behavior (KV cache warmup). sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' - we're calling it KV cache.
[00:14:02] Marcus: we'll also note quantization behaviors across model families.
[00:14:07] Tom: on the UI side, marketplace wants a deep link to a sample app; do you have a one-click deploy sample?
[00:14:13] Jordan: we have a sample docker-compose and helm chart. we'll add a one-click link per Velos marketplace requirements.
[00:14:20] Aisha: perfect. anything else?
[00:14:23] Lena: one final compliance ask - can we get a SOC2 letter and the last pen test summary sanitized for public listing?
[00:14:30] Marcus: yes we'll prepare the sanitized pen test summary and SOC2 attestation.
[00:14:35] [00:14:45] -- short discussion about roles --
[00:15:05] Jordan: quick recap of action items: Priya to draft reference arch and manifest; Marcus to attach security docs; Tom to provision staging; Diego to share network rules; Lena to send compliance checklist; Jordan to coordinate benchmarks and send sample terraform. correct?
[00:15:25] Aisha: yep that matches.
[00:15:28] Tom: i'll set up the staging and send creds to priya and jordan.
[00:15:33] Diego: i'll provide a CIDR and list of IPs for egress.
[00:15:37] Priya: i'll have the reference arch and manifest by 2026-03-18 and put in a shared drive link.
[00:15:43] Marcus: security docs will be sent by end of week.
[00:15:46] Lena: checklist by 2026-03-19.
[00:15:50] Jordan: ok last thing - any competitors to be aware of on the Velos marketplace?
[00:15:55] Aisha: there are two strong players, MegaCloud and GigaServe, but we prefer partners who can provide both hosted and private options.
[00:16:05] Jordan: good to know. thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email with links.
[00:16:12] Aisha: thanks, bye.
[00:16:14] Tom: bye.
[00:16:16] Diego: thanks.
[00:16:18] [end of recorded transcript]

Note: transcript contains occasional minor transcription errors typical of auto-generated meeting notes (e.g., 'radwood' for 'redwood', 'KV cash' for 'KV cache').
